research_spec.competing_explanation: Any observed gain could come from added parameters or regularization pressure rather than exclusion semantics. Diagnostic summaries showing whether the exclusion gate activates non-trivially across users rather than collapsing near zero for the whole run.
Per-user or per-item-stratum evaluation indicating whether any benefit concentrates on harder negatives, substitute-rich regions, or tail items consistent with the exclusion-memory rationale.
research_spec.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if the exclusion-enabled model does not beat the matched mechanism-off control on full-sort NDCG@10, or if the learned exclusion gate remains effectively unused/collapsed so that behavior is indistinguishable from the control despite successful optimization.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This diagnosis proposal directly addresses the accepted gap by forcing an isolatable wedge with an explicit executable mechanism-off, rather than adding another entangled variant whose effect cannot be separated from backbone or training differences.

research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-relation scoring architecture with separate attraction and exclusion item spaces. research_spec.closest_parent: Explicitly learning a user-conditioned exclusion memory and subtractive gate alongside standard attraction embeddings will improve ranking quality because many hard negatives are not merely low-affinity items; they are items that align with patterns the user's history implicitly avoids.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any improvement would come only from extra parameters or generic regularization rather than from modeling an explicit exclusion relation.
discriminative_predictions: A parameter-matched control that adds a second user embedding through additive fusion instead of subtractive exclusion will underperform the proposed mechanism if the exclusion relation is the operative cause.

Replacing user-specific exclusion memory with a single global exclusion vector should remove most of the gain while keeping similar regularization pressure, indicating the effect is not just extra capacity.

The proposed model should show larger relative improvement for users whose histories span nearby but conflicting item neighborhoods, whereas a generic-capacity explanation predicts more uniform gains across users.

research_spec.falsifier: If a parameter-matched additive control or global-exclusion control matches or exceeds the proposed model on NDCG@10, the exclusion-relation hypothesis is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: The proposal introduces an explicit second user-item relation with subtractive scoring semantics and dedicated updates from negative evidence, which changes the representational object from single compatibility to attraction-plus-opposition rather than merely retuning an existing operator.
